advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Build the corpus/material index once per sweep and reuse it across criteria instead of rebuilding per attempt.
evidence: `_ProductionAttempter._criterion_rows` caches rows per criterion but the corpus build inside `_run_admission`/`_material_index` is re-invoked on every `run()`
advisory.finding: `_select_rows` and `_material_index` each independently call `corpus.build_corpus` over the whole tracker for every criterion attempt, rebuilding the same corpus repeatedly within one sweep.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a loop-level test: run heal_fixtures three times over one criterion with AttemptResult(outcome=INCOMPLETE) and assert the counter does not accrue and no unreliable-criterion ticket is filed (unreliable_titles(store) == [], report.quarantined == ()).
evidence: heal.py _fold_outcome has NO branch for AttemptOutcome.INCOMPLETE — it silently falls through all three `if` blocks (lines 301-313), so an INCOMPLETE outcome relies on absence-of-code to leave the counter unchanged; a regression that added INCOMPLETE to the FAILED_REPRODUCE/SKIPPED_UNBALANCED tuple would file a spurious quarantine ticket after 3 outages.

Contract quote (heal.py module docstring): 'INCOMPLETE — a transient outage ... Leave the counter UNCHANGED and neither admit nor quarantine, so a passing outage does not accrue toward a spurious quarantine'

test_fixture_heal_heldout.py:252 test_incomplete_admission_is_not_a_reproduction_failure asserts only `result.outcome == "incomplete"` from `_ProductionAttempter.run` — it never invokes heal_fixtures, so the loop's counter/quarantine handling of INCOMPLETE is unexercised.
ABSENCE: search of tests/unit for INCOMPLETE loop coverage finds no heal_fixtures run with repeated INCOMPLETE outcomes asserting unreliable_titles(store) == [] after >= threshold runs.
advisory.finding: The INCOMPLETE disposition's loop-level contract ('leave the counter UNCHANGED and neither admit nor quarantine, so a passing outage does not accrue toward a spurious quarantine') is untested at the heal_fixtures loop level. Only the _ProductionAttempter.run classification (that it returns 'incomplete') is covered; no test drives heal_fixtures with repeated INCOMPLETE results to prove no counter accrual / no quarantine ticket.
scenarios: A regression that folds INCOMPLETE into the failure-counter branch would file an unreliable-criterion ticket for a criterion whose only problem was 3 transient LLM/infra outages; no test would catch it.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_fixture_heal_heldout.py add test_incomplete_outcome_never_accrues_quarantine: use FakeAttempter returning AttemptResult(outcome=AttemptOutcome.INCOMPLETE) via run_at across days 0/30/60 and assert unreliable_titles(store) == [] and report.quarantined == () on every run.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Populate CaseOutcome.usage_rows from eval_solver.run_case output so real admission spend is recorded to the ledger and the cumulative $25 cap is enforced.
evidence: fixture_admission.py:192: `usage_rows.extend(rows)` and fixture_admission.py:230 finalize `usage_rows` — the solver's usage_rows is the sole spend channel into the ledger

Ticket contract: 'a subsequent reserve re-checks cumulative actual spend, so an actual that overran its estimate makes the NEXT reserve raise BudgetExceeded' — impossible when actual spend is never finalized
heal.py:200: `if result.usage_rows:` — the loop's own finalize is also skipped because the production AttemptResult carries no usage_rows
blocking.finding: The live admission solver hardcodes `usage_rows=[]`, so actual model token spend from `eval_solver.run_case` is never recorded to the ledger; the $25 cumulative-spend cap the loop relies on cannot see real cost and fails open.
blocking.suggested_fix: Extract the per-call usage rows from `output` (as the sibling reference solver does) and pass them into `CaseOutcome(..., usage_rows=<rows>)` instead of `[]`.
